title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: space and CQL filters for what the Confluence connectors index
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, filtering behaviour, prerequisites and licensing statements are supported. Minor corrections should complete the navigation paths and acknowledge that the checklist also names access permissions and limited-audience rollout controls that are absent from the table.

claims.where: What's changing: Status and differences between sources; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap describes simplified Cloud filters for page ID, creation date/time and last update date/time.
claims.quote: For Confluence Cloud connector, it introduces simplified options to filter pages by page id, creation date/time and last update date/time

claims.where: What's changing: Status and differences between sources
claims.claim: The roadmap describes advanced CQL filtering for the On-premises connector.
claims.quote: For Confluence On-premises connector, it adds support for advanced CQL-based filtering, enabling more complex and flexible filtering scenarios.

claims.claim: The Confluence Cloud connector brings indexed Confluence pages and blogs into Copilot and Microsoft Search.
claims.quote: The Confluence Cloud Microsoft 365 Copilot connector integrates Confluence content into Microsoft 365, enabling Copilot, Copilot Search, and Microsoft Search to surface relevant wiki pages and blogs

claims.claim: The On-premises connector indexes self-hosted Confluence Data Center or Server content for Microsoft Search and Copilot.
claims.quote: The Confluence On-premises connector enables Microsoft 365 to index and retrieve content from self-hosted Confluence Data Center or Server instances. It brings enterprise wiki content into Microsoft Search and Copilot

claims.claim: The Cloud connector indexes all blogs and pages by default.
claims.quote: By default, the Confluence Cloud connector indexes all blogs and pages.

claims.claim: Admins can include or exclude Cloud spaces from indexing.
claims.quote: You can include or exclude spaces that you want to index.

claims.where: What's changing: Confluence Cloud; summary; Why it matters; controls[0].governs
claims.claim: A Cloud CQL string restricts which pages sync, including by modification date.
claims.quote: For advanced scenarios, use a Confluence Query Language (CQL) string to specify conditions for syncing pages. For example, you can choose to index only the pages that were modified in the last two years.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents lastModified >= "2024/12/31" as an example CQL date filter.
claims.quote: You can use the CQL filter to index content modified after a certain time by using, for example, `lastModified >= "2024/12/31"`.

claims.quote: Choose **Preview results** to verify the sample values of the selected properties and CQL string.

claims.claim: On-premises connections can include or exclude spaces by space key.
claims.quote: Include or exclude specific spaces by using the space filter option. Each space has a space key identifier that forms part of the URL for that space.

claims.where: What's changing: Status and differences between sources; Open questions
claims.claim: The Cloud deployment page does not document separate page ID or date filter fields as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Confluence Cloud connector simplified page ID creation date last update date filter'; read Cloud deployment content settings and Cloud service setup search excerpts. They document space selection and CQL, not separate page ID or date filter fields.

claims.claim: The Cloud filter is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Connectors > Gallery > Confluence Cloud > Custom setup > Include or exclude data.
claims.quote: Choose the **Connectors** tab, and in the left pane, choose **Gallery**.
claims.fix: Include the intervening content-settings heading: 'Copilot > Connectors > Connectors > Gallery > Confluence Cloud > Custom setup > Customize content settings > Include or exclude data', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/confluence-cloud-deployment.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for setting the Microsoft-built Confluence Cloud connector's space or CQL filters.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Confluence Cloud On-premises connector configure CQL space filters Microsoft Graph API PowerShell'; read Cloud deployment, service-setup excerpts and Graph externalConnection reference. Source-side search APIs do not configure the Microsoft-built connector; no filter-setting call found.

claims.claim: On-premises filter setup is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Gallery > Confluence On-premises > Custom setup.
claims.quote: To customize settings, on the connector page in the admin center, select **Custom setup**.
claims.fix: Complete the path to the documented filter section: 'Copilot > Connectors > Gallery > Confluence On-premises > Custom setup > Customize content settings', at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/confluence-onpremises-deployment.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table; Open questions

claims.quote: Searched: 'Confluence Cloud On-premises connector configure CQL space filters Microsoft Graph API PowerShell'; read On-premises deployment and overview, source-setup search excerpts, and Graph externalConnection reference. No operation configuring these connector filters was found.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: By default, indexed results respect users' existing access in Confluence rather than making content visible to everyone.
claims.quote: Only people with access to this data source (default)

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Everyone access setting exposes the connection's indexed data in search results to all users.
claims.quote: If you choose **Everyone**, indexed data appears in the search results for all users.

claims.claim: Permission updates synchronize only during full crawls.
claims.quote: Updates to permissions sync only during full crawls.

claims.claim: Full crawls run daily, every 24 hours, by default.
claims.quote: By default, full crawls run every 24 hours.

claims.claim: Content filters coexist with the connectors' identity mapping and permission settings rather than replacing them.
claims.quote: If you choose **Only people with access to this data source**, search results respect the same permission setup as the data source.

claims.claim: Microsoft's manage-connections guidance says to delete and recreate a connection with an exclusion filter to stop indexing unwanted items.
claims.quote: To update this connection, first delete the existing connection and create a new one with a data source exclusion filter that excludes the items you no longer want to index.

claims.claim: The filters are included under the connector's existing Microsoft 365 licensing rather than a separately documented filter entitlement.
claims.quote: Indexing of synced connector data incurs no extra cost for tenants with Microsoft 365 licenses.
